title: AST SpaceMobile Stock (ASTS) Rises 14.1% on Rakuten Venture (Nov 9)
summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) closed at $36.89 on Nov 9, up 14.10%, as media tied the gain to its Rakuten joint venture in Japan. Q3 results came after the close.
body_markdown:
## Why AST SpaceMobile Stock Rose


According to[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-ast-spacemobile-stock-jumped-233502515.html) , the stock rose on the joint venture with Rakuten, a partner since 2020. The venture, Rakuten AST, will be controlled by Rakuten and use AST's satellites to extend cell service to areas with poor coverage and to keep people connected during disasters.


Per AST SpaceMobile's[quarterly report filed with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780312/000119312526453759/asts-20260930.htm) , the two companies agreed on November 6, 2026 to set up Rakuten AST in Japan, with Rakuten holding 51% of the voting shares and AST 49%. The filing says Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications selected the Rakuten-led proposal for its J-LEO satellite project, and the venture expects a grant of up to JPY 148.0 billion, about $938.0 million, over roughly three years. AST will supply the satellites and receive a one-time software license fee of $75.0 million. The Motley Fool noted that the government funding itself had been known since a June bid.


Third-quarter results came after the close, so the[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) did not drive the session. According to the company's[third-quarter release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526453758/asts-ex99_1.htm) , revenue rose to $42.3 million from $14.7 million a year earlier, and the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $132.4 million, or $0.44 per share. As reported by[Investing.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ast-spacemobile-misses-estimates-shares-230148893.html) , revenue fell short of the $47.9 million analysts expected, and the loss was wider than the $0.40 per share consensus.


## ASTS Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- The Rakuten AST venture gives AST a satellite supply agreement and a one-time $75.0 million license fee, per the 10-Q.
- The company kept its full-year revenue guidance of $150.0 million to $200.0 million and held about $3.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, according to its release.
- AST says it is targeting about 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid-2027 and nationwide intermittent service in the US and other key markets before the end of 2026.


### Risks


- Q3 revenue and loss per share both missed analyst estimates, per Investing.com, and the company remains loss-making.
- Its plans depend on launches, and the 10-Q flags the risk that AST may not be able to launch its satellites, or operate them after launch, successfully.
- The 10-Q also discloses a putative securities class action filed on September 14, 2026, plus two derivative lawsuits filed on October 21 and November 5, 2026.
